failures.criterion: Spec item 1: front-door pods keep their own state and certificates come from the stored Secret under the 3-per-7-days claim budget. A pod's claim gate must keep deciding on every pass whatever the ledger annotations hold.
failures.evidence: Red test TestDispatchCertificateBudgetSkipsAMalformedEpoch (packages/envoy/infra/gcp/dispatch_frontdoor_test.go, commit b0af6aa9). Command: `cd packages/envoy/infra && go test ./gcp/ -run TestDispatchCertificateBudget -count=1`. Result: `--- FAIL: TestDispatchCertificateBudgetSkipsAMalformedEpoch ... /bin/sh: 91: Illegal number: 09`. Every other TestDispatchCertificateBudget* test passes. Cause: dispatch_frontdoor.go:377 and :389 accept any digits-only epoch (`case "$t" in ''|*[!0-9]*)`), and the arithmetic at :378 and :390 reads a leading zero as octal (it fails on 8 or 9; `0177` silently becomes 127), and dash fails on more than 19 digits. The shell error ends the gate's background subshell `( ... ) &`. Nothing restarts it, and the cert-publish container stays alive. So every pod that reads that ledger (all of them share one Secret) never advertises and stays unready until a person edits the annotation. The implementer's tests feed no such epoch. Check that a fix works: skipping `0*` and 20-digit epochs at both lines makes the test pass (tried locally, then reverted).

observations: Low severity and outside the red test: annotation() in dispatch_frontdoor.go:315 puts the key unescaped into a sed regex. A decoy key such as `legionxdev/certificate-claims` that sorts after the real one is read in its place, and the gate then overwrites 3 live claims. A value that holds an escaped quote is cut at the backslash, the gate's merge patch becomes invalid JSON, and the gate gets 400 on every pass. Only a person editing the Secret by hand can cause either.

The listener on main answers /healthz 200 {"status":"starting"} before NATS connects, and exits 10 s later if NATS stays unreachable (cmd/listener/main.go log.Fatal). INFRA-557 owns that; it is unchanged here.

At SIGTERM, Go's Server.Shutdown closes idle keep-alive connections with no response, and only a response already in flight carries Connection: close. The preStop sleep 5 is what covers callers. This matches the implementer's T9.2 deviation in substance.
